subject: math
title: Decimal Place Value, Powers of 10, Comparing and Rounding Decimals
seo_title: Grade 5 Decimal Place Value Worksheets: Thousandths, Powers of 10 and Exponents, Comparing and Rounding Decimals
domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standard_text: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left. Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10, and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10. Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths. Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 decimal place value worksheets: value of a digit to thousandths, 10 times and 1/10 as much, powers of 10 with exponents, word form and expanded form, comparing and ordering decimals, and rounding with number lines. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. Line up the decimal points to compare, and look one place to the right to round.
key_sub: 0.7 is 10 times 0.07. 10<sup>3</sup> = 1,000 moves the point 3 places. 0.5 > 0.125 even with fewer digits, and 3.995 rounds to 4.00 at the nearest hundredth.
body_html:
Each place is 10 times the place to its right

Moving one place to the left makes a digit worth 10 times as much. Moving one place to the right makes it worth 110 as much. This works on both sides of the decimal point.

Places to the right of the point end in -ths: tenths, hundredths, thousandths. A thousandth is tiny (0.001); a thousand is big (1,000).

Powers of 10 and exponents

The exponent tells how many 10s are multiplied. It is also the number of zeros.

Power of 10MeansValueMultiply: point movesDivide: point moves
10110101 place right1 place left
10210 × 101002 places right2 places left
10310 × 10 × 101,0003 places right3 places left
10410 × 10 × 10 × 1010,0004 places right4 places left
Example

36 × 102 and 4.7 ÷ 102

× 100: the point moves 2 places right: 36 → 3,600. ÷ 100: the point moves 2 places left: 4.7 → 0.047.

Answer: 3,600 and 0.047

Three ways to write a decimal

Form3.045
Standard form3.045
Word formthree and forty-five thousandths
Expanded form3 × 1 + 4 × 1100 + 5 × 11,000

In word form, say “and” only for the decimal point. Read the digits after the point as a whole number, then name the last place: 0.045 is forty-five thousandths.

Compare decimals

Line up the decimal points. Write zeros at the end so both numbers have the same number of places. Then compare from the left.

Compare

0.5 ☐ 0.502

0.5 = 0.500. Tenths: 5 = 5. Hundredths: 0 = 0. Thousandths: 0 < 2.

Answer: 0.5 < 0.502

Round decimals

  1. Find the place you are rounding to.
  2. Look at the digit just to its right.
  3. 5 or more: round up. 4 or less: keep the digit.
  4. Drop the digits after the rounding place.
Round 6.849 to the nearestLook atAnswer
whole number8 tenths7
tenth4 hundredths6.8
hundredth9 thousandths6.85
Watch the 9s

Round 3.995 to the nearest hundredth.

The hundredths digit is 9 and the next digit is 5, so round up: 3.99 + 0.01 = 4.00. Keep both zeros.

Answer: 4.00

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
0.125 > 0.5 because it has more digitsCompare place by place: 0.125 < 0.500
Reading 0.045 as forty-five hundredthsName the last place: forty-five thousandths
103 = 30103 = 10 × 10 × 10 = 1,000
4.7 ÷ 100 = 470Dividing makes it smaller: move the point left, 0.047
6.849 → 6.85 → 6.9Look only at the next digit: 6.8
Rounding 3.995 to 3.99 (cutting off digits)Round up when the next digit is 5 or more: 4.00

faq.q: How do you read decimals to the thousandths?
faq.a: Say the whole number, say “and” for the decimal point, read the digits after the point as a whole number, then name the last place. 3.045 is “three and forty-five thousandths”.

faq.q: How do you compare decimals like 0.5 and 0.49?
faq.a: Write them with the same number of places (0.50 and 0.49) and compare from the left. 5 tenths is more than 4 tenths, so 0.5 > 0.49, even though 0.49 has more digits.

faq.q: What is an exponent in 5th grade math?
faq.a: An exponent shows how many 10s are multiplied: 10<sup>3</sup> = 10 × 10 × 10 = 1,000. Multiplying by 10<sup>3</sup> moves the decimal point 3 places to the right; dividing moves it 3 places to the left.

faq.q: How do you round a decimal to the nearest hundredth?
faq.a: Look at the thousandths digit. If it is 5 or more, add 1 to the hundredths digit; if it is 4 or less, keep it. 2.736 rounds to 2.74, and 3.995 rounds to 4.00.

sets.title: Value of a digit, 10 times and 1/10 as much

items.q: What is the value of the digit 3 in this number?
items.e: The 3 is the 1st digit after the point, in the tenths place. Its value is 3 tenths = 3 × 110 = 0.3.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in this number?
items.e: The 4 is the 2nd digit after the point, in the hundredths place. Its value is 4 hundredths = 4 × 1100 = 0.04.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 9 in this number?
items.e: The 9 is the 3rd digit after the point, in the thousandths place. Its value is 9 thousandths = 9 × 11,000 = 0.009.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in this number?
items.e: The 7 is in the tens place, so its value is 7 × 10 = 70.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in this number?
items.e: The 8 is the 2nd digit after the point, in the hundredths place. Its value is 8 hundredths = 8 × 1100 = 0.08.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in this number?
items.e: The 7 is the 3rd digit after the point, in the thousandths place. Its value is 7 thousandths = 7 × 11,000 = 0.007.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in 31.284?
items.e: The 4 is the 3rd digit after the point, in the thousandths place. Its value is 4 thousandths = 4 × 11,000 = 0.004.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 6 in 9.065?
items.e: The 6 is the 2nd digit after the point, in the hundredths place. Its value is 6 hundredths = 6 × 1100 = 0.06.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 1 in 142.39?
items.e: The 1 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 1 × 100 = 100.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 9 in 0.917?
items.e: The 9 is the 1st digit after the point, in the tenths place. Its value is 9 tenths = 9 × 110 = 0.9.

items.q: In 8.305, which place is the digit 5 in?
items.e: Places to the right of the point end in -ths: tenths, hundredths, thousandths. Places to the left do not: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands. The 5 is in the thousandths place.

items.q: In 2,416.7, which place is the digit 4 in?
items.e: Places to the right of the point end in -ths: tenths, hundredths, thousandths. Places to the left do not: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands. The 4 is in the hundreds place.

items.q: In 0.628, which place is the digit 2 in?
items.e: Places to the right of the point end in -ths: tenths, hundredths, thousandths. Places to the left do not: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands. The 2 is in the hundredths place.

items.q: In 5.55, how does the 5 in the tenths place compare to the 5 in the hundredths place?
items.e: The tenths 5 is 0.5 and the hundredths 5 is 0.05. 0.5 = 10 × 0.05, so it is worth 10 times as much. One place to the left is always 10 times as much.

items.q: In 3.333, how does the 3 in the thousandths place compare to the 3 in the hundredths place?
items.e: The thousandths 3 is 0.003 and the hundredths 3 is 0.03. 0.003 is 0.03 ÷ 10, so it is worth 110 as much. One place to the right is always 110 as much.

items.q: What is 10 times as much as 0.03?
items.e: 10 times as much moves each digit 1 place to the left: 3 hundredths become 3 tenths, 0.3. Writing a 0 at the end (0.030) does not change the value.

items.q: What is 110 of 0.4?
items.e: 110 of a number moves each digit 1 place to the right: 4 tenths become 4 hundredths, 0.04. (4 is 10 times as much, and 0.40 is the same as 0.4.)

items.q: 0.6 is 10 times as much as what number?
items.e: 10 times what is 0.6? One place to the right of tenths is hundredths: 0.06. Check: 10 × 0.06 = 0.6.

items.q: How many hundredths are in 0.3?
items.e: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 3 tenths = 30 hundredths. 0.3 = 0.30.

items.q: How many thousandths make 1 hundredth?
items.e: Each place is 10 times the place to its right, so 10 thousandths make 1 hundredth: 10 × 0.001 = 0.01.

items.q: What is 10<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: The exponent 3 tells how many 10s are multiplied: 10 × 10 × 10. So 103 is 1 followed by 3 zeros: 1,000. It is not 10 × 3 = 30.

items.q: What is 10<sup>4</sup>?
items.e: The exponent 4 tells how many 10s are multiplied: 10 × 10 × 10 × 10. So 104 is 1 followed by 4 zeros: 10,000. It is not 10 × 4 = 40.

items.q: What is 10<sup>6</sup>?
items.e: The exponent 6 tells how many 10s are multiplied: 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 × 10. So 106 is 1 followed by 6 zeros: 1,000,000. It is not 10 × 6 = 60.

items.q: Which shows 100,000 using an exponent?
items.e: 100,000 is 1 followed by 5 zeros, so it is 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 = 105. Count the zeros, not all 6 digits.

items.q: Which is the same as 10 × 10 × 10 × 10?
items.e: Four 10s are multiplied, so the exponent is 4: 104 = 10,000. (40 is 10 + 10 + 10 + 10.)

items.q: What is 36 × 10<sup>2</sup>?
items.e: 102 = 100, which has 2 zeros. Multiplying by 102 moves the decimal point 2 places to the right: 36 × 102 = 3,600. Write zeros to fill the empty places. (720 comes from thinking 102 = 20.)

items.q: What is 7 × 10<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: 103 = 1,000, which has 3 zeros. Multiplying by 103 moves the decimal point 3 places to the right: 7 × 103 = 7,000. Write zeros to fill the empty places. (21 comes from multiplying by 3 instead of 1,000.)

items.q: What is 450 × 10<sup>2</sup>?
items.e: 102 = 100, which has 2 zeros. Multiplying by 102 moves the decimal point 2 places to the right: 450 × 102 = 45,000. Write zeros to fill the empty places. (900 comes from multiplying by 2 instead of 100.)

items.q: What is 2.5 × 10<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: 103 = 1,000, which has 3 zeros. Multiplying by 103 moves the decimal point 3 places to the right: 2.5 × 103 = 2,500. Write zeros to fill the empty places. (2.5000 only adds zeros after the point, and that does not change the value.)

items.q: What is 0.68 × 10<sup>2</sup>?
items.e: 102 = 100, which has 2 zeros. Multiplying by 102 moves the decimal point 2 places to the right: 0.68 × 102 = 68.

items.q: What is 3.9 × 10<sup>2</sup>?
items.e: 102 = 100, which has 2 zeros. Multiplying by 102 moves the decimal point 2 places to the right: 3.9 × 102 = 390. Write zeros to fill the empty places. (3.900 only adds zeros at the end and does not change the value.)

items.q: What is 0.05 × 10<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: 103 = 1,000, which has 3 zeros. Multiplying by 103 moves the decimal point 3 places to the right: 0.05 × 103 = 50. Write zeros to fill the empty places.

items.q: What is 1.24 × 10<sup>1</sup>?
items.e: 101 = 10, which has 1 zero. Multiplying by 101 moves the decimal point 1 place to the right: 1.24 × 101 = 12.4. (1.240 only adds zeros at the end and does not change the value.)

items.q: What is 4.7 ÷ 10<sup>2</sup>?
items.e: 102 = 100. Dividing by 102 moves the decimal point 2 places to the left: 4.7 ÷ 102 = 0.047. Write zeros to hold the empty places. Check: dividing makes the number smaller.

items.q: What is 365 ÷ 10<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: 103 = 1,000. Dividing by 103 moves the decimal point 3 places to the left: 365 ÷ 103 = 0.365. Write zeros to hold the empty places. Check: dividing makes the number smaller.

items.q: What is 82 ÷ 10<sup>2</sup>?
items.e: 102 = 100. Dividing by 102 moves the decimal point 2 places to the left: 82 ÷ 102 = 0.82. Write zeros to hold the empty places. Check: dividing makes the number smaller.

items.q: What is 5 ÷ 10<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: 103 = 1,000. Dividing by 103 moves the decimal point 3 places to the left: 5 ÷ 103 = 0.005. Write zeros to hold the empty places. Check: dividing makes the number smaller.

items.q: How many zeros are at the end of the product 40 × 10<sup>3</sup>?
items.e: 103 = 1,000 gives 3 zeros, and 40 already has 1 zero. 40 × 1,000 = 40,000, which has 4 zeros at the end. (7 adds 4 + 3, and 3 forgets the zero in 40.)

items.q: To find 4.7 ÷ 10<sup>2</sup>, how does the decimal point move?
items.e: The exponent 2 means ÷ 100, so the point moves 2 places. Dividing makes the number smaller, so it moves to the left: 4.7 → 0.47 → 0.047.

items.q: What goes in the box? 0.093 × ☐ = 93
items.e: 0.093 → 0.93 → 9.3 → 93: the point moved 3 places to the right, so the number was multiplied by 1,000 = 103. (102 would give 9.3.)

sets.title: Read and write decimals: word form and expanded form

items.q: Write in standard form: twelve and six hundredths
items.e: “And” marks the decimal point. Hundredths need 2 digits after the point, so write a 0 in the tenths place. So twelve and six hundredths is 12.06.

items.q: Write in standard form: three and forty-five thousandths
items.e: “And” marks the decimal point. Thousandths need 3 digits after the point: 045. “Thousandths” is not “thousands”. So three and forty-five thousandths is 3.045.

items.q: Write in standard form: two hundred eight thousandths
items.e: “And” marks the decimal point. There is no “and”, so there is no whole number part. Thousandths need 3 digits: 208. So two hundred eight thousandths is 0.208. (200.008 would be “two hundred and eight thousandths”.)

items.q: Write in standard form: fifty and nine thousandths
items.e: “And” marks the decimal point. Thousandths need 3 digits after the point, so write two zeros first: 009. So fifty and nine thousandths is 50.009.

items.q: Write in standard form: six and three hundred four thousandths
items.e: “And” marks the decimal point. Thousandths need 3 digits after the point: 304. So six and three hundred four thousandths is 6.304.

items.q: Write in standard form: six and fifteen thousandths
items.e: “And” marks the decimal point. Thousandths need 3 digits after the point: 015. So six and fifteen thousandths is 6.015.

items.q: Which is 0.045 in word form?
items.e: The last digit, 5, is in the thousandths place, so read 45 and say thousandths. So it is forty-five thousandths.

items.q: Which is 2.07 in word form?
items.e: Say the whole number, say “and” for the point, then read 07 as seven and name the last place: hundredths. So it is two and seven hundredths.

items.q: Which is 13.502 in word form?
c: thirteen and five hundred two thousandths
thirteen and five hundred twenty thousandths
thirteen and five hundred two hundredths
items.e: Read the digits after the point as a whole number (502), then name the last place: thousandths. So it is thirteen and five hundred two thousandths.

items.q: Which is 4.38 in word form?
items.e: Read the digits after the point as a whole number (38), then name the last place: hundredths. So it is four and thirty-eight hundredths.

items.q: Which is 0.909 in word form?
items.e: Read 909, then name the last place: thousandths. Do not say “and” inside 909: “and” means the decimal point, so “nine hundred and nine thousandths” is 900.009. So it is nine hundred nine thousandths.

items.q: Which shows 4.326 in expanded form?
c: 4 × 1 + 6 × 110 + 2 × 1100 + 3 × 11,000
4 × 1 + 3 × 110 + 2 × 1100 + 6 × 11,000
4 × 10 + 3 × 1 + 2 × 110 + 6 × 1100
items.e: Write each non-zero digit times the value of its place: 4 × 1 + 3 × 110 + 2 × 1100 + 6 × 11,000. A 0 adds nothing, but it still holds its place, so the digits after it stay in the right places.

items.q: Which shows 0.507 in expanded form?
c: 5 × 110 + 7 × 11,000
5 × 110 + 7 × 1100
5 × 1100 + 7 × 11,000
items.e: Write each non-zero digit times the value of its place: 5 × 110 + 7 × 11,000. A 0 adds nothing, but it still holds its place, so the digits after it stay in the right places.

items.q: Which shows 12.08 in expanded form?
c: 1 × 1 + 2 × 110 + 8 × 11,000
items.e: Write each non-zero digit times the value of its place: 1 × 10 + 2 × 1 + 8 × 1100. A 0 adds nothing, but it still holds its place, so the digits after it stay in the right places.

items.q: What number is 5 × 10 + 2 × 1 + 6 × 1100?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place between them: 5 tens 2 ones 6 hundredths = 52.06.

items.q: What number is 7 × 1 + 3 × 11,000?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place between them: 7 ones 3 thousandths = 7.003. 11,000 means thousandths, not thousands.

items.q: What number is 9 × 110 + 4 × 11,000?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place between them: 9 tenths 4 thousandths = 0.904. 11,000 means thousandths, not thousands.

items.q: Which number has 2 ones, 0 tenths, 5 hundredths and 8 thousandths?
items.e: Write the digits in order after the point: 0 tenths, 5 hundredths, 8 thousandths → 2.058. Keep the 0 in the tenths place.

items.q: Which number has a 6 in the thousandths place?
items.e: The thousandths place is the 3rd digit after the point. In 5.236 it is 6. In 6,235 the 6 is in the thousands place, not the thousandths.

items.q: Which number is equal to 0.4?
items.e: Zeros at the end of a decimal do not change its value: 0.4 = 0.40 = 0.400. Zeros right after the point do: 0.04 and 0.004 are much smaller.

sets.title: Compare and order decimals to thousandths

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Line up the decimal points and write zeros so all have 3 places: 0.700, 0.650, 0.698, 0.069. Then compare from the left. 0.700 and 0.698 first differ in the tenths place: 7 > 6. So 0.7 is the greatest. More digits does not mean greater.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Line up the decimal points and write zeros so all have 3 places: 2.350, 2.305, 2.400, 2.399. Then compare from the left. 2.400 and 2.399 first differ in the tenths place: 4 > 3. So 2.4 is the greatest. More digits does not mean greater.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Line up the decimal points and write zeros so all have 3 places: 0.500, 0.490, 0.502, 0.499. Then compare from the left. 0.502 and 0.500 first differ in the thousandths place: 2 > 0. So 0.502 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Line up the decimal points and write zeros so all have 3 places: 8.090, 8.100, 8.009, 8.099. Then compare from the left. 8.100 and 8.099 first differ in the tenths place: 1 > 0. So 8.1 is the greatest. More digits does not mean greater.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Line up the decimal points and write zeros so all have 3 places: 0.300, 0.250, 0.209, 0.310. Then compare from the left. 0.250 and 0.209 first differ in the hundredths place: 5 > 0. So 0.209 is the least.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Line up the decimal points and write zeros so all have 3 places: 1.080, 1.800, 1.008, 1.081. Then compare from the left. 1.080 and 1.008 first differ in the hundredths place: 8 > 0. So 1.008 is the least.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Line up the decimal points and write zeros so all have 3 places: 4.600, 4.060, 4.606, 4.066. Then compare from the left. 4.066 and 4.060 first differ in the thousandths place: 6 > 0. So 4.06 is the least.

items.q: Which comparison is true?
items.e: Write both with the same number of places: 0.125 and 0.500. The first different place is the tenths: 1 and 5. So 0.125 < 0.5. 0.125 has more digits, but it is still less.

items.q: Which comparison is true?
items.e: Write both with the same number of places: 3.070 and 3.068. The first different place is the hundredths: 7 and 6. So 3.07 > 3.068. 3.068 has more digits, but it is still less.

items.q: Which comparison is true?
items.e: Write both with the same number of places: 0.900 and 0.899. The first different place is the tenths: 9 and 8. So 0.9 > 0.899. 0.899 has more digits, but it is still less.

items.q: Which comparison is true?
items.e: Zeros at the end do not change a decimal: 6.420 is 6 ones, 4 tenths, 2 hundredths, the same as 6.42. So 6.42 = 6.420.

items.q: Which comparison is true?
items.e: Write both with the same number of places: 12.305 and 12.350. The first different place is the hundredths: 0 and 5. So 12.305 < 12.35. 12.305 has more digits, but it is still less.

items.q: Rain fell on three days: 0.35 in., 0.305 in. and 0.4 in. Which list shows them from least to greatest?
items.e: Write them with the same number of places: 0.350, 0.305, 0.400. Compare from the left. Order: 0.305, 0.35, 0.4. The number with more digits is not always greater.

items.q: Three long jumps measured 3.08 m, 3.8 m and 3.18 m. Which list shows them from least to greatest?
items.e: Write them with the same number of places: 3.08, 3.80, 3.18. Compare from the left. Order: 3.08, 3.18, 3.8. The number with more digits is not always greater.

items.q: Three beetles are 1.25 cm, 1.205 cm and 1.3 cm long. Which list shows them from least to greatest?
items.e: Write them with the same number of places: 1.250, 1.205, 1.300. Compare from the left. Order: 1.205, 1.25, 1.3. The number with more digits is not always greater.

items.q: In a 60-meter race, three runners finished in 9.87 seconds, 9.8 seconds and 9.807 seconds. Which list shows them from least to greatest?
items.e: Write them with the same number of places: 9.870, 9.800, 9.807. Compare from the left. Order: 9.8, 9.807, 9.87. The number with more digits is not always greater.

items.q: Three apples weigh 0.215 kg, 0.25 kg and 0.2 kg. Which list shows them from greatest to least?
items.e: Write them with the same number of places: 0.215, 0.250, 0.200. Compare from the left. Order: 0.25, 0.215, 0.2. The number with more digits is not always greater.

items.q: Which number is between 0.6 and 0.7?
items.e: 0.6 = 0.60 and 0.7 = 0.70. A number between them has 6 tenths and more after it: 0.68 = 6 tenths 8 hundredths. 0.068 has 0 tenths, so it is less than 0.6.

items.q: Ava says 0.125 is greater than 0.5 because 125 is greater than 5. Is she right?
items.e: Compare place by place, not the digits as whole numbers. 0.5 = 0.500. Tenths: 1 < 5, so 0.125 < 0.5. Ava is not right.

items.q: Which number is not equal to 0.7?
items.e: 0.70 and 0.700 only add zeros at the end, and 710 is 7 tenths, so they all equal 0.7. 0.07 is 7 hundredths, 10 times smaller.

items.q: Round 3.46 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 3.46 is between 3.4 and 3.5. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 3.5.

items.q: Round 7.38 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: To the nearest whole number, 7.38 is between 7 and 8. Look at the digit just to the right of the ones place: 3. 3 is less than 5, so round down. Answer: 7.

items.q: Round 2.735 to the nearest hundredth.
items.e: To the nearest hundredth, 2.735 is between 2.73 and 2.74. Look at the digit just to the right of the hundredths place: 5. It is exactly halfway, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 2.74.

items.q: Round 0.65 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 0.65 is between 0.6 and 0.7. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 5. It is exactly halfway, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 0.7.

items.q: Round 4.96 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 4.96 is between 4.9 and 5.0. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. The tenths digit is 9, so adding 1 regroups: 4.9 + 0.1 = 5.0. Answer: 5.0. Keep the 0 at the end to show the number is rounded to the tenth.

items.q: Round 3.995 to the nearest hundredth.
items.e: To the nearest hundredth, 3.995 is between 3.99 and 4.00. Look at the digit just to the right of the hundredths place: 5. It is exactly halfway, and 5 rounds up. The hundredths digit is 9, so adding 1 regroups: 3.99 + 0.01 = 4.00. Answer: 4.00. Keep the 0 at the end to show the number is rounded to the hundredth.

items.q: Round 6.849 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 6.849 is between 6.8 and 6.9. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 4. 4 is less than 5, so round down. Answer: 6.8. Do not round in steps (6.849 → 6.85 → 6.9). Look only at the hundredths digit.

items.q: Round 0.462 to the nearest hundredth.
items.e: To the nearest hundredth, 0.462 is between 0.46 and 0.47. Look at the digit just to the right of the hundredths place: 2. 2 is less than 5, so round down. Answer: 0.46.

items.q: Round 12.508 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: To the nearest whole number, 12.508 is between 12 and 13. Look at the digit just to the right of the ones place: 5. 5 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 13.

items.q: Round 9.96 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 9.96 is between 9.9 and 10.0. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. The tenths digit is 9, so adding 1 regroups: 9.9 + 0.1 = 10.0. Answer: 10.0. Keep the 0 at the end to show the number is rounded to the tenth.

items.q: Round 0.073 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 0.073 is between 0.0 and 0.1. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 7. 7 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 0.1.

items.q: A swimmer's time was 14.387 seconds. What is the time rounded to the nearest hundredth of a second?
items.e: To the nearest hundredth, 14.387 is between 14.38 and 14.39. Look at the digit just to the right of the hundredths place: 7. 7 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 14.39.

items.q: Gas costs $3.459 per gallon. What is the price rounded to the nearest cent (hundredth of a dollar)?
items.e: To the nearest hundredth, 3.459 is between 3.45 and 3.46. Look at the digit just to the right of the hundredths place: 9. 9 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: $3.46. A cent is a hundredth of a dollar.

items.q: Eli's pencil is 17.65 cm long. How long is it to the nearest whole centimeter?
items.e: To the nearest whole number, 17.65 is between 17 and 18. Look at the digit just to the right of the ones place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 18.

items.q: A puppy weighs 4.548 kg. What is its weight rounded to the nearest tenth of a kilogram?
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 4.548 is between 4.5 and 4.6. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 4. 4 is less than 5, so round down. Answer: 4.5. Do not round in steps (4.548 → 4.55 → 4.6).

items.q: A trail is 2.96 miles long. What is its length to the nearest tenth of a mile?
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 2.96 is between 2.9 and 3.0. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. The tenths digit is 9, so adding 1 regroups: 2.9 + 0.1 = 3.0. Answer: 3.0. Keep the 0 at the end to show the number is rounded to the tenth.

items.q: This month, 3.075 inches of rain fell. What is that rounded to the nearest hundredth of an inch?
items.e: To the nearest hundredth, 3.075 is between 3.07 and 3.08. Look at the digit just to the right of the hundredths place: 5. It is exactly halfway, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 3.08.

items.q: A runner finished a race in 58.249 seconds. What is the time to the nearest tenth of a second?
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 58.249 is between 58.2 and 58.3. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 4. 4 is less than 5, so round down. Answer: 58.2. Do not round in steps (58.249 → 58.25 → 58.3).

items.q: A bag of nuts weighs about 1.3 lb, rounded to the nearest tenth. Which could be the exact weight?
items.e: Numbers from 1.25 up to (but not including) 1.35 round to 1.3. 1.26 is in that range. 1.35 and 1.39 round up to 1.4, and 1.24 rounds down to 1.2.

items.q: A scale shows 6.482 kg. A label rounds it to 6.5 kg. To which place was it rounded?
items.e: 6.5 has one digit after the point, so it is rounded to the nearest tenth: 6.482 is between 6.4 and 6.5, and the hundredths digit is 8, so it rounds up to 6.5. To the nearest hundredth it would be 6.48, and to the nearest whole number 6.
